business_scope.primary_industry_name: Product Interface Design and Digital Design Subscription Agency

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between the Republic of Korea and the United Kingdom for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income

Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendations as implemented by the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Information (Act No. 18934, effective 2021), the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Information, and the Commercial Act (Act No. 17905). Beneficial ownership identification and verification obligations are imposed on financial institutions under Article 5-2 of the Act, requiring the collection of UBO data for all legal entities. The Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) and the National Tax Service (NTS) have statutory access to such information.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Foreign Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the country of origin (e.g., Companies House in the UK, Secretary of State in the US)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a local notary public in the country of origin, followed by Apostille issuance by the designated competent authority (e.g., Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office in the UK, Secretary of State in the US) pursuant to the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961, which the Republic of Korea acceded to on July 14, 2007. No consular legalization is required.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Foreign Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry or tax authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Apostille as per the Hague Apostille Convention, as described above. The certificate must be issued within 90 days prior to submission.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation of the Korean subsidiary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the resolution or PoA by a notary public in the country of origin, followed by Apostille issuance by the competent authority. The document must be in English or accompanied by a certified Korean translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or Memorandum) of the Foreign Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry or legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Apostille as per the Hague Apostille Convention. The document must be certified as a true copy by the issuing authority.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Foreign Parent Company's Principal Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Apostille as per the Hague Apostille Convention. The letter must be dated within 90 days and confirm the parent company's financial standing and banking relationship.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit's (KoFIU) list of designated persons. Additionally, enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Information, including foreign PEPs, domestic senior officials, and their family members and close associates. Screening must be conducted at onboarding and on a continuous basis using real-time automated systems. Any adverse match triggers immediate suspension of the incorporation process and a suspicious transaction report (STR) to KoFIU within 24 hours. The screening protocol must also include negative news checks and adverse media monitoring, with a documented risk-based approach for low-risk design subscription businesses.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office (Internet Registration System) - www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Korean script (Hangul). Foreign names may be transliterated phonetically into Hangul. The name must include the corporate form suffix '주식회사' (Chusik Hoesa). The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered company name or trademark. The four-tier naming convention comprises: (1) corporate form, (2) trade name, (3) business purpose, and (4) location. The name must be distinguishable from existing names in the same registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Supreme Court Registry Office within 14 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a written statement explaining why the name should be accepted, along with evidence of non-conflict with existing names and trademarks. The Registry Office must respond within 30 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Administrative Court. Alternatively, the applicant may modify the name and resubmit the application. It is recommended to conduct a preliminary name search using the IROS portal and to reserve the name before filing the incorporation documents to avoid delays.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permitted for registration purposes, but the National Tax Service (NTS) and financial institutions may reject a virtual office if it is merely a commercial mailbox without a physical presence. For a design subscription company, a virtual office may be acceptable if it includes a physical address, a receptionist, and meeting rooms. However, banks such as those used for Stripe Billing and Wise may require a physical address for corporate account opening. The NTS may conduct on-site inspections to verify the existence of the registered office. It is recommended to lease a serviced office or a physical office space to ensure compliance and avoid bank account rejection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) NTS may conduct unannounced inspections to verify the registered office address. (2) The registry office may also verify the address during incorporation. (3) Banks may require a site visit before account opening. Likelihood: Moderate for a low-risk design company, quantified at 30% if a virtual office is used, and 10% if a physical office is leased. The risk increases if the company is registered at a commercial mailbox address without a physical presence.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Court Registration Tax (Registration Tax and Education Surtax)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff based on 0.4% of capital, with a minimum fee of KRW 200,000 (approx. USD 150) for companies with no minimum capital requirement.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Stamp Duty on Articles of Incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory stamp duty of KRW 50,000 (approx. USD 50) for incorporation documents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal Fees for Incorporation and Drafting of Articles of Incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard Chusik Hoesa incorporation with no complex share classes, ranging from USD 1,200 to USD 2,000.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary Fees for Certification of Articles of Incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary tariff based on the notarization of the articles of incorporation, typically KRW 100,000 (approx. USD 100).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille Fees for Foreign Parent Documents (5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority in the country of origin (e.g., Secretary of State, Foreign Office)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate of USD 50 per document for apostille issuance, totaling USD 250 for five documents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Virtual Office or Serviced Office Address (First Year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a virtual office with physical address and meeting room access in Seoul, ranging from USD 400 to USD 600 per year.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank Account Opening Assistance and Compliance Support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for assistance with corporate bank account opening, including KYC documentation preparation and liaison with banks, typically USD 150 to USD 300.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended); applicable provisions for a Chusik Hoesa include Articles 288 to 328 (formation), Article 289 (contents of Articles of Incorporation), Articles 290 to 296 (subscription and payment for shares), Article 305 (deposit of subscription price), Article 312 (statutory auditor threshold), Article 316 (inaugural board meeting), Article 317 (registration of incorporation), and Articles 383 to 408 (board of directors and officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local District Court Registry Office (Deunggi-gwa) of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office; administrative oversight by the Supreme Court of Korea's Registration Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Jeonggwan) together with an Application for Corporation Registration and all statutory attachments filed through the court's electronic registration system or at the District Court Registry counter
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa; therefore no blocked escrow account or mandatory capital deposit guarantee is legally required. However, the entire subscription price for all issued shares must be fully paid in before incorporation registration, either in cash deposited at a designated financial institution or through an approved in-kind contribution valuation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IN THE MATTER OF [COMPANY NAME] CHUSIK HOESA; RESOLUTION OF THE INAUGURAL MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS. WHEREAS, [COMPANY NAME] Chusik Hoesa (a stock corporation) was organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea by promoters who subscribed for the initial shares and prepared the Articles of Incorporation; and WHEREAS the Articles have been notarized, the shares subscribed in full, and the subscription price deposited with a designated bank in accordance with Article 305 of the Commercial Act, which has issued a certificate of paid-in capital; and WHEREAS the subscribers have appointed the undersigned directors as the first board, and no statutory auditor is required because the paid-in capital does not exceed the statutory threshold; and WHEREAS the directors are required by Article 316 and their fiduciary duties to hold an inaugural board meeting and to ratify the incorporation transactions. NOW, THEREFORE, the directors, being the entire board, voting unanimously, adopt the following resolutions: (1) Share Capital and Allotment. The board acknowledges the subscription forms and the capital deposit certificate, ratifies the allotment of [NUMBER] ordinary shares at a par value of KRW [PAR VALUE] each, and confirms the aggregate paid-in capital of KRW [TOTAL], paid in full in cash or in approved in-kind contribution. (2) Banking Authorizations. The board designates [BANK NAME] as its principal depositary; authorizes the representative director, jointly with a second signatory, to open and operate operating accounts, foreign exchange accounts, and settlement accounts for Stripe Billing and Wise; execute bank mandates; and approve routine transactions. (3) Registered Office Adoption. The board adopts the address in the Articles as the registered office and authorizes the representative director to evidence premises authorization and register the company. (4) Statutory Officers. The board appoints [NAME] as representative director, [NAME] as inside director, and [NAME] as company secretary. Officers shall act within the powers of the Act and Articles. (5) Registration. The board authorizes the representative director to file the incorporation registration with the District Court Registry and the business registration with the National Tax Service, and to take all ancillary steps. This resolution is binding on the Company; the company secretary shall transcribe it into the minute book and provide certified copies to banks, payment processors, and government agencies. Adopted at [CITY] on [DATE] by unanimous vote.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and formalization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public authorized under the Korean Notary Public Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Promoters must draft the Articles of Incorporation in accordance with Article 289 of the Commercial Act, including an object clause covering professional design and digital UI/UX services, share par value, number of authorized shares, contribution methods, registered office address, corporate duration, and promoters' names. The promoters must attend the notary office in person, present identification, and sign the final version. The notary verifies capacities and procedural completeness, reads the instrument, and issues a notarized certificate. Any amendment after notarization must be approved and executed contemporaneously before filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation signed by all promoters
Government-issued photo identification of each promoter
Business plan or object clause description for ISIC 7410 design services
Proof of proposed registered office address if already identified
Notarized power of attorney if a promoter is represented by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the document for incomplete shareholder information or ambiguous capital provisions, the promoters must submit a revised Articles text, obtain a written correction note from the notary, and re-submit for notarization within five business days without reopening share subscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share subscription and payment of initial capital at a designated financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated commercial bank acting as the subscription payment institution under Article 291 of the Commercial Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After delivery of the notarized Articles, promoters must make the subscription offer by creating a share subscription form setting forth the total number of shares to be issued, issue price, par value, payment date, and bank designation. Subscribers execute the subscription form and pay the full issue price into a temporary account opened at the designated bank. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit confirming receipt of the paid-in subscription amount. The promoters must retain original subscription forms and the bank's capital deposit certificate for submission to the court. In-kind contributions, if any, must be inspected by an appraiser appointed by the promoters in accordance with the Act.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Stock subscription forms completed and signed by each subscriber
Corporate bank deposit receipts or certificate of paid-in capital issued by the designated bank
Valuation certificate if in-kind contribution is made
Identification documents for bank customer due diligence and AML clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank customer due diligence or AML review causes delay, the promoters should provide a source-of-funds declaration and business profile. If the bank rejects the subscription because of missing corporate documents, the promoters may select another licensed bank. Any underpayment must be cured by transfer of the deficit before registration; otherwise the court may question the incorporation registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convening and adoption of the inaugural board resolution and appointment of statutory officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inaugural board of directors of the corporation consisting of all initial directors appointed by subscribers; no external government authority is involved
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon verification of capital deposit, the initial directors must convene a formal first board meeting. Notice must be given to each director, and the meeting must be attended by a majority of the directors. The directors should pass a first board resolution in formal written form, approving the share allotment, adopting the registered office, opening bank accounts, and appointing the representative director and any other statutory officers. Board minutes must be prepared, signed by the chairperson and each present director, and kept in the corporate minute book. Where a statutory auditor is required under the Act because subscribed capital exceeds a threshold, the auditor's appointment must also be confirmed at the same meeting.
required_dossiers: Notice of board meeting and attendance register
Inaugural board resolution text
Directors' written acceptances of appointment
Certified copy of notarized Articles
Bank certificate of paid-in capital
List of directors and auditor with resident registration numbers and addresses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any director lacks capacity or a conflict of interest is alleged, the resolution must be reconvened with a properly cleared director. If the meeting cannot achieve a quorum, an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders may appoint substitute directors, and the resolution must be re-signed accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation registration with the District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registry Office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the Company's registered office, operated under the Supreme Court of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The representative director or a legal agent must file the incorporation registration using the court's electronic registration system or in-person counter filing. The application must include an executed registration statement in the prescribed statutory form, the notarized Articles, the bank certificate of deposit of subscription amount, the minutes of the inaugural board meeting, and evidence of the paid-up capital. The registry officer reviews the submission for conformity with Articles 289 to 317, including the object clause, share system, directors' qualifications, and office address. Upon favorable review, the registry assigns a corporate registration number and enters the formation into the commercial registry. The incorporation takes effect at the time of registration.
required_dossiers: Application for corporation registration in the official court form
Notarized original Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate of paid-in capital or valuation report
Minutes of the inaugural board meeting
Form attesting to the designation of directors and statutory auditor if any
Power of attorney if filing by an agent
Certificate of payment of registration tax and local education tax
Consent of the property owner or building usage certificate for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a demand for supplementation due to defective documents, the deficiency must be cured within two weeks by submitting amended forms or supplementary affidavits. If the registration is suspended for suspected falsified capital, the applicant may submit bank reconciliation statements or convert to a cash-only subscription. An appeal or re-filing may be made through the court's non-contentious case procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation business registration and tax and design-service compliance filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through its online HomeTax portal and the local district tax office with jurisdiction over the business premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court registers the Chusik Hoesa, the representative director must apply for a business registration certificate from the local tax office within twenty days from the incorporation date. The application must state the ISIC 7410 specialized design activity, the office address, and expected turnover. The National Tax Service will issue a corporate tax identification number and VAT registration status. Additionally, the company should open wage and remittance accounts and submit the statutory business commencement notice. Because the activity is a pure design subscription service, no separate industrial permit is required; however, the company should retain the business-registration certificate to obtain a tax clearance certificate for banking and foreign payment gateway onboarding.
required_dossiers: Incorporation registration certificate and court-issued corporate registration number
Notarized copy of Articles or certified extract of the commercial registry
Application for business registration in the prescribed tax office form
Lease agreement or office use agreement for the registered address
Corporate seal registration certificate if required by the tax office
Director's identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service queries the business scope or address, the company must file an amended registration explaining the ISIC 7410 digital design subscription scope. A late-filing penalty can be mitigated by demonstrating a timely intended filing date, making the missing filing immediately, and paying any minor administrative fine within the statutory cure period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. No separate industrial licensing board is engaged for ISIC 7410 digital UI/UX design subscription services because the activity does not involve physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No operating license or manufacturing permit is required for a Chusik Hoesa engaged in digital design and subscription services under the Commercial Act or Korea's industrial convergence regulations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable. No Environmental Impact Assessment tier applies because the business is purely digital design services with no physical development, site alteration, or large-scale resource consumption.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. No quantitative wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste emission thresholds apply to the digital design subscription activity. If the company later leases large-scale server or data-center facilities, it must reassess applicable energy-use reporting and e-waste disposal obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable. No civil defense fire-safety permit, structural load inspection, or special workplace approval is triggered by a pure design subscription business. The company remains subject to general fire safety obligations for its office lease and, as an employer, to the Occupational Safety and Health Act for routine administrative work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea, via the HomeTax electronic portal at www.hometax.go.kr; Korea Customs Service for export declarations and customs clearance data.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity engaged in taxable supplies in Korea must register with the National Tax Service by filing a business registration application through HomeTax or with the competent local tax office, appointing a domestic tax representative if no place of business exists in Korea. The applicant submits a certified copy of the foreign registration certificate (apostilled or consular-legalized as applicable), the entity's articles of incorporation or constitutional documents, a power of attorney evidencing the tax representative, and supporting identification documents. Upon completion, NTS assigns a 10-digit business registration number which also serves as the Korean VAT identification number, and issues the business registration certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not provide a check-the-box election or separate hybrid mismatch entity elections under the Korean Corporate Tax Act or VAT Act. A Chusik Hoesa is inherently treated as a Korean domestic corporation taxed at entity level, and foreign-incorporated entities are classified as foreign corporations unless the place of effective management or head office is in Korea.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act and its Enforcement Decree
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general KRW registration threshold for foreign non-resident taxable suppliers; any taxable supply of goods or services in Korea triggers VAT registration. For domestic businesses, annual taxable turnover under KRW 80,000,000 may qualify for simplified taxable person status, but a Chusik Hoesa operating as a legal person is generally classified as a general taxable person.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All general taxable persons must issue electronic tax invoices for every taxable supply and transmit them to NTS through HomeTax by the end of the business day following the supply date. Korea does not apply physical fiscal stamps; NTS performs near-real-time clearance and data matching against customs, payment card, and bank transaction records. ERP integration and API-based bulk submission via HomeTax are mandatory standards for high-volume taxpayers, and all tax invoices remain subject to NTS digital audit and reconciliation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, zero rating applies to exported goods and to services supplied to non-resident enterprises, including cross-border digital design and UI/UX subscription services. Services qualify when the recipient is a foreign non-resident entity, the place of supply is overseas, the service is actually used or reviewed outside Korea, and the consideration is received in foreign currency. A zero-rated electronic tax invoice must be issued and the exporter must retain all export, transport, service delivery, and foreign exchange receipt evidence to substantiate the claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service (export declaration/Bill of Entry equivalent for exported services supported by service contract and use certificate for goods zero-rating where applicable)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill or equivalent transport documentary evidence for physical exports, plus proof of overseas delivery for digital service supply

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank, or a bank-confirmed foreign exchange receipt statement evidencing actual collection of export proceeds in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If zero-rating is claimed without actual export or foreign exchange receipt, NTS reverses the zero-rating, claws back any refunded input VAT, and applies additional VAT under the VAT Act: 40% for fraudulent or false invoicing and 20% for negligent under-reporting, plus interest. Criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may be pursued, carrying up to 3 years imprisonment or fines up to KRW 30 million. False or overstated export declarations also expose the entity to Korea Customs Service administrative penalties, revocation of export facilitation status, and retrospective reassessments throughout the statutory audit period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as central bank; Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as foreign-exchange administrative authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) as banking and AML supervisory enforcement agency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a legally open but carefully reported foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is fully convertible for virtually all current-account transactions, including trade-related design subscription fees, royalties, operating profits, software service payments and ordinary operating expenses. Such payments pass through designated foreign exchange banks without prior approval, subject to post-trade reporting requirements triggered by thresholds that vary by transaction type and delegated commercial-bank authority. Capital and financial account operations, however, are regulated: inbound equity injections, shareholder loans, dividends, loan drawdowns and capital repatriation must have a legal transaction basis, and in practice require either prior declaration to MOEF or the use of a designated foreign exchange bank that files the required Foreign Exchange Information System records. Dividends and profit remittances are fully permitted for a foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa, but the bank will demand certified audited financial statements, tax payment/deduction completion certificates, corporate authorization documents and evidence of the original foreign investment registration. Although the won floats freely and BOK does not impose surrender quotas, practical convertibility is conditional on clean KYC files, accurate purpose codes and full supporting documentation. Offshore investors holding KRW exposure generally find the onshore market liquid for USD, EUR and JPY, but exotic cross-currency corridors require pre-confirmed bank pricing and internal compliance approval. Overall, the KRW regime is considered open on the current account and administratively gatekept on the capital account, meaning high but not unconditional convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and related delegated rules, an exporter of goods or services must collect export proceeds through a designated foreign exchange bank in Korea and receive those proceeds into a Korean bank account. The statutory collection period is generally six months from the date the export occurs, and exporters must obtain the bank's confirmation that the export settlement has been made. There is no mandatory conversion ratio under current Korean rules; proceeds may be retained in a Foreign Currency Deposit Account or converted to KRW at the market rate. Late collection without a justifiable reason can trigger penalty procedures and additional documentary scrutiny. Exceptions or extensions may be permitted by the bank where payment is delayed by third-party credit events, disputes, or other commercial grounds demonstrated with supporting evidence.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational KRW Currency Account
Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational KRW Currency Account
Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational KRW Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary treasury and clearing rail. A non-resident fintech EMI such as Wise is not legally authorized in South Korea to hold corporate client funds as a domestic licensed bank or to provide a local KRW transactional current account to a Chusik Hoesa unless it obtains registration under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and a business relationship with a licensed Korean bank. Foreign EMIs may be used only as a supplementary non-KRW payment or collection channel where the local partner is FSS-registered and where the service does not involve capital escrow, FDI inflows, statutory profits, or corporate bank account opening. Therefore, this blueprint mandates a Tier-1 domestic commercial bank for all statutory treasury and capital account movements, and treats EMI rails as ancilliary low-value payment options only after separate legal validation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is required. Under Korea's Real Name Financial Transactions Act and FSS AML guidance, the statutory representative director or an in-country authorized signatory holding a properly notarized power of attorney must appear in person at a branch of the chosen commercial bank to complete identity verification. Remote video KYC and consular proxy opening are not generally accepted for a first corporate banking relationship, because the bank must independently verify the identity documents, corporate seal, beneficial owners and the commercial substance of the applicant. Some banks permit a second signatory or supporting staff to be onboarded via video after the primary director has been physically verified, but the initial account opening is branch-based. The UI/UX design subscription entity should expect a face-to-face AML interview covering expected transaction patterns, client geography, revenue model, service delivery evidence, and non-resident ownership structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated Chusik Hoesa with 100% non-resident beneficial ownership and a Design-as-a-Service subscription revenue model may be treated as a potential shell company without local operational substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled company constitution, business registration certificate, entity ledger, local office lease agreement with utility invoices, employment contracts for local UI/UX designers, project delivery logs, customer contracts, and a board resolution authorising the account opening. The dossier must also include UBO passports, residence permits, and a detailed local operational questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound foreign equity capital injection triggers Foreign Investment Promotion Act reporting and capital verification; the bank may reject if the remittance lacks a clear legal basis or if the investor's source of wealth cannot be documented.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Report certificate issued by KOTRA or the designated foreign exchange bank, foreign currency remittance certificate, investor-side bank statements covering the full remittance amount, tax returns, sale deeds or liquidation records proving source of wealth, board resolution approving share allotment, and a written capital investment plan linked to the company's design subscription business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border related-party service fees for design subscription work may raise trade misinvoicing, transfer pricing, or disguised royalty remittance concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master service agreements with clear scope, delivery milestones, fee schedules, service levels, and termination clauses; itemised invoices with project codes; actual delivery evidence such as Figma project IDs, Git commit histories, Slack/email correspondence, completion certificates; and arm's length transfer pricing documentation prepared by a licensed Korean tax advisor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Name screening of non-resident shareholders, Korean directors, or subscribed corporate clients may trigger sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media alarms, causing an extended compliance review or denial.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed beneficial ownership schedule, certified copies of passports for all 25% or greater shareholders and registered directors, signed sanctions/PEP self-declaration forms, country-specific adverse-media explanations, public-source search evidence for each flagged name, tax identification numbers, and a commitment letter to provide purpose codes and underlying contracts for all MT103 transactions within bank review timelines.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign investor capital must be wired by MT103 from the investor's own account to the designated foreign exchange bank in Korea, referencing the beneficiary company name, Chusik Hoesa registration number, and the purpose code for foreign direct investment. The remittance narrative must identify the share subscription and the Foreign-Invested Enterprise registration or FDI filing number. The receiving bank credits the foreign currency account, issues a certificate of receipt, and supports conversion to KRW at the prevailing market rate. Capital verification is achieved through the Foreign Investment Registration certificate, the bank-issued certificate of foreign currency deposit, and the notice of share allotment. After completion, the company must update the Foreign Exchange Information System via the bank and retain remittance slips, BOJ/Customs reports, and board resolutions for internal AML audit and future dividend repatriation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For digital design subscription services, SWIFT MT103 is the primary clearing rail for outbound disbursements such as overseas contractor payments, cloud licensing, royalty distributions, and operating fees. The remitter must submit the underlying master service agreement, invoice, and evidence of service delivery, and must use the correct non-trade service payment purpose code when filing with the Korean bank. Commercial letters of credit are usable only when the company exports or imports physical goods in its ancillary supply chain; documentary collections such as DP/DA may also be deployed for goods-backed trade. For all outbound current account payments, the company must retain complete supporting files for at least five years and must answer any bank inquiry within the stipulated time frame to avoid delayed reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD and KRW/EUR forward contracts with exposure confirmation, underlying invoice, and a bank-approved hedging line for committed current-account payables and receivables

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where the counterparty is non-resident and the transaction hedges a genuine Korean won exposure arising from real trade or foreign investment; speculative NDF use by domestic residents is not advisable and is generally restricted

Cross-currency swaps for prudential asset-liability matching on foreign-currency borrowings or capital structures, subject to bank credit approval and clear evidence of underlying balance-sheet exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and shareholder approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external government filing; notice and minutes kept at the registered head office and available to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year, the Annual General Meeting must be held no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to convene the Annual General Meeting or fail to prepare and provide the statutory financial statements may be subject to commercial administrative fines of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,800); continued inactivity and non-filing may lead to cancellation of the business registration and court-ordered dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return on the verified tax base
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the third month after fiscal year-end; a December 31 fiscal year is due March 31 of the following year, subject to a prescribed one-month extension in limited cases
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing additional tax of 20% of the deficient corporate tax, underreporting additional tax of 10%, plus late-payment interest at approximately 0.022% per day (about 8.0% annualized) until full payment; chronic default may result in NTS estimated assessment, asset attachment, cancellation of business registration, and judicial dissolution proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax surcharge return on the annual corporate income tax liability
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local tax authority of the Si/Gun/Gu in which the registered head office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after fiscal year-end; a December 31 fiscal year is due April 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing and underreporting additional taxes plus statutory late-payment interest at approximately 0.022% per day accrue under the Local Tax Act; overdue balances are subject to lien registration, attachment, and compulsory collection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited annual financial statements and independent statutory auditor's report for companies that meet an audit threshold or are designated as audit targets
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit report must be delivered to the company before the Annual General Meeting; audited financial statements must be submitted to FSS/KICPA within 14 days after Annual General Meeting approval; for a December 31 fiscal year, the practical final deadline is normally April 14 following a March 31 Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit within the statutory period may result in corrective orders, administrative fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, auditor designation by the FSS, and public sanctions against the company and responsible directors

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% top marginal rate on taxable income above KRW 300 billion; otherwise 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, and 24% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion under Corporate Tax Act Article 55
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small and medium enterprise reduced rates under Article 55-2, R&D tax credits and employment promotion credit under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, foreign investment tax holiday under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, free economic zone and foreign investment zone three-year/five-year corporate tax exemptions, and tax credits for job creation and facility investment

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return and Local Income Tax Return schedules, filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax system (hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; preliminary interim corporate tax return due for the first six months of a fiscal year under Corporate Tax Act Article 61
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end, e.g., for a December 31 year-end the filing and payment deadline is March 31 of the following year; extension of up to two months is available only through HomeTax application before the original filing deadline

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification: legal name, business registration number, representative director, business location, fiscal year start and end dates, and foreign shareholder details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose every non-resident shareholder holding 5% or more of the shares, the non-resident shareholder's jurisdiction of tax residence, permanent establishment or agent status, and ensure the Korean company remains a domestic corporation under Korean domestic law; if a foreign director or foreign service provider issues instructions, record the economic substance of decision-making to avoid classification as a second head office or permanent establishment of the foreign owner

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement reconciliation: revenue, cost of goods or service provision, gross profit, selling and administrative expenses, operating income, non-operating income and expense, and pre-tax book income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accrue UI/UX design subscription revenue over the subscription term in accordance with Korean tax accounting standards; do not net out payment processing fees from Stripe or Wise; separately allocate digital design service fees from foreign related parties and maintain contracts, delivery records, and time logs to substantiate the cross-border service charge; exclude output VAT and include only corporate-taxable operating revenue

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment schedule: non-deductible expenses, non-taxable income, depreciation differences, entertainment expenses, related-party transaction adjustments, and other book-to-tax reconciliation entries
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back royalties or design service fees paid to offshore shell companies that lack beneficial ownership and real operations; make transfer pricing adjustments when intercompany subscriptions, license fees, or service charges are not at arm's length; restrict deduction of excessive agency fees paid to non-residents; and document the business purpose of any offshore invoicing or payment processing arrangement

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation, application of progressive corporate tax rates, and the national corporate income tax charge before credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute national corporate income tax on the entire taxable base of the Korean Chusik Hoesa; do not allocate worldwide income of non-resident shareholders; validate the applicable progressive bracket using the annual taxable income and then add the local income tax surcharge of 10% of the national corporate tax within the same filing

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits and deductions: foreign tax credits, R&D tax credits, employment tax credits, minimum tax credits, and any prior-period loss carryforwards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Substantiate foreign tax credits only with official tax payment certificates from the country generating the foreign-sourced income; do not claim treaty withholding tax on outbound dividends or royalties as a corporate income tax credit because those are shareholder-level or per-payment taxes; coordinate the loss carryforward schedule carefully because the Korean tax law may only permit a 10-year carryforward with future taxable income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax payable and refund position: national corporate tax, local income tax surcharge, advance payments, interim tax payments, and final balance due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the final sum remitted to a single payment account equals national corporate tax plus the 10% local income tax surcharge; before declaring any dividend, calculate separately the shareholder-level withholding tax due for non-resident shareholders at the aggregate 22% statutory rate (20% national withholding plus 2% local income tax), and continue to report outbound dividend withholdings on the periodic withholding return rather than within the corporate income tax return

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an additional tax of 10% of the tax payable on a non-filed return, 20% for under-reported income and 40% for fraudulent or dishonest filing; unpaid corporate tax accrues a daily surcharge of 0.022% for each overdue day up to a maximum of 36 months; failure to file of the corporate income tax return may also trigger the same obligations for the local income tax surcharge; intentional non-filing or false filing constitutes tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, carrying imprisonment up to 10 years or a fine of up to five times the evaded tax, and can lead to NTS blacklisting and travel restrictions

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate statutory rate composed of 20% national withholding tax under Corporate Tax Act Article 98 plus 2% local income tax surcharge; reduced rates may apply under a bilateral DTA
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before remitting a dividend, interest, or royalty offshore, the non-resident payee must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its jurisdiction of residence, provide a beneficial ownership declaration confirming that the payee is the true economic owner and not a nominee, and submit the appropriate application for treaty-based withholding tax exemption or reduction to the National Tax Service or the Korean withholding agent; the Korean payer must retain the TRC, beneficial ownership evidence, board resolutions, royalty or license agreements, and proof that the non-resident entity has substantive business activity and decision-making functions; treaty relief will be denied if the non-resident fails the Principal Purpose Test or is a bare conduit in a zero-tax jurisdiction, requiring the full 22% statutory withholding; a refund application may be filed with the district tax office if excessive withholding has already been remitted
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest on intercompany loans is generally subject to 22% aggregate statutory withholding (20% national plus 2% local), with treaty rates usually ranging from 5% to 15%; royalties for intellectual property, trademarks, and UI/UX design software are likewise subject to 22% statutory withholding, though DTAs may reduce or exempt royalties; only actual and substantiated arm's length royalty and interest payments are deductible and only if the Korean payer has obtained the relevant withholding tax certificate, underlying contract, TRC, and beneficial ownership file

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10,000,000,000 in annual aggregate cross-border related-party transactions within the calculation period is the statutory threshold requiring preparation and submission of Master File and Local File documentation under the Act on Coordination of International Tax Affairs; lower transactional values may nevertheless be audited and adjusted by the Korean National Tax Service
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korean domestic tax law does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations to ordinary Korean limited companies, but the substance-over-form doctrine and General Anti-Abuse Rules are embedded in Korean case law and in Article 121 of the Framework Act on Taxation; for DTA relief and withholding tax reductions, the Korean tax authorities require the non-resident payee to carry on Core Income-Generating Activities in its residence state, having its own office, employees, real decision-making authority, and economic risk; shell companies, letterbox entities, and conduits are disregarded and treated as non-beneficial owners, permitting the Korean authorities to deny treaty benefits and impose the full statutory withholding rate

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Korean Chusik Hoesa intentionally omits UI/UX design subscription revenue, issues false or inflated invoices, conceals offshore receivables held through Stripe or Wise, fails to file the annual corporate income tax return despite generating taxable revenue, or under-declares taxable income after the first fiscal year-end
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evasion Act Article 3: imprisonment up to 10 years or fine not exceeding five times the amount of evaded national tax; additional 40% fraudulent filing penalty, 20% under-reporting penalty, daily unpaid tax surcharge of 0.022%, and full local income tax surcharge liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the entity is used as a sham or the directors personally caused the evasion, the Korean tax authorities may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors jointly liable for unpaid corporate tax, local tax, penalties and surcharges; the directors may be blacklisted as dishonest taxpayers, subjected to travel suspension, have personal assets attached, and face criminal imprisonment up to 10 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing And Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean design subscription company pays large royalty or intercompany service fees to a related Hong Kong, Singapore, or BVI entity that has no employees, no office, no board meetings, and no real business function; the arrangement lacks a transfer pricing study and is designed only to shift Korean profits offshore before the annual filing and distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Act on Coordination of International Tax Affairs Articles 4 through 6, the Korean National Tax Service may adjust the intercompany transaction to an arm's length amount, disallow the excessive deduction, impose transfer pricing adjustment penalties and interest, and if the arrangement is fraudulent, convert excess payments into constructive dividends subject to 22% withholding tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who deliberately sign sham related-party agreements and route money through shell entities can be treated as receiving disguised dividends or embezzling corporate assets; Korean courts may pierce the corporate veil where the company is a mere instrumentality and make directors personally liable for investor restitution, repatriation of diverted funds, the entire tax deficiency, travel bans, blacklisting, and imprisonment for tax evasion if the scheme is criminalized

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse, AML And Beneficial Ownership Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Korean Chusik Hoesa is controlled by an undisclosed non-resident who uses nominee Korean directors, has no Korean office or payroll, has no commercial substance, and uses Stripe Billing and Wise only to collect global subscription fees; the Korean company is a shell designed to mask the ultimate beneficial owner and to obtain treaty benefits that would otherwise be unavailable
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Real Name Financial Transaction Act requires disclosure of beneficial ownership, and violations may result in administrative fines, criminal fines, and penal consequences; the Korean tax authority can disregard the shell entity, tax the controlling non-resident on the Korean-source design subscription income, and deny all DTA benefits; the Framework Act on Taxation imposes joint liability for unpaid tax on the interventionist non-resident and the nominal Korean directors
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee and de facto directors are both at risk; the corporate veil can be pierced if the company is a façade, leading to personal civil liability for unpaid Korean taxes, restitution to creditors, disgorgement of payments made through payment facilitators, travel restrictions and blacklisting by the National Tax Service, and criminal imprisonment for participation in tax evasion or falsification of the corporate record, with a potential sentence of up to 10 years under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act
